review.instruction: Verify the concrete evidence actually contradicts the challenged rule in its declared case and comes from the same relevant surface or family. A consumer preference or single unexplained mismatch is insufficient.

Confirm the repair occurs in the one canonical owner and chooses correction of an existing rule before adding a concept. Reject duplicated thresholds, consumer patches, generated-file edits and unrelated cleanup.
Compare before and after authority. Existing rule identifiers retain their address and meaning unless explicitly retired to a named survivor; new cases append without renumbering.

Require the post-repair manifest and response to name the originating operation, exact surface/reference and current owner bytes for a fresh rerun. The repair itself cannot claim visual or behavioral acceptance.

failurePolicy: Inspect evidence, repair the smallest canonical owner, rebuild the manifest and reassess. Concrete feedback returns to evidence selection or the owner edit. An unchanged repeated challenge stops rather than rewriting the rule again.
